💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alejandro Garnacho is yet to start a game for Aston Villa this season.
  • Alejandro Garnacho's time at Aston Villa has been brief - and it already looks to be over.
  • The latest snub by Villa boss Unai Emery was the most damming of all, with the on-loan Chelsea winger left out of Tuesday's Champions League defeat at Galatasaray.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alejandro Garnacho is yet to start a game for Aston Villa this season.

Alejandro Garnacho's time at Aston Villa has been brief - and it already looks to be over.

The latest snub by Villa boss Unai Emery was the most damming of all, with the on-loan Chelsea winger left out of Tuesday's Champions League defeat at Galatasaray.

"The players who were here I think are the best players to be here with us," remarked Emery.

Villa could have had 12 substitutes in Istanbul but Emery chose just 11 - including two goalkeepers - as Garnacho stayed at home.

The plan was for the Argentina international's loan move to become permanent for Â£43m should certain criteria be met.

They are believed to be based on a number of appearances staff felt were so achievable the club were in little doubt he would become a Villa player.

But now there is doubt he will ever play for them again.

Garnacho trained with Villa's first team on Monday but did not travel to Istanbul.

"First start after three months. Happy to be enjoying football again.".

The post Garnacho wrote on social media after a pre-season game in July has - along with anything else related to Villa - been deleted from his account.

He has played just 34 minutes in the Premier League this season, and seven of Villa's 11 games ended without him getting on the pitch.

His last appearance - just a three-minute cameo - came in the 1-1 draw against Fulham on 31 October.

Including Saturday's 0-0 draw with Sunderland, Garnacho has been omitted from the past three matchday squads - a strong sign Emery has lost faith in him.

But he may have been fighting a losing battle from the off, having arrived at Villa unfit.

Sources have acknowledged the 22-year-old was not at the level required and were surprised how off the pace he was when he signed in July.

He initially trained on his own, and questions over the signing were already being asked, with eyebrows raised by some internally given his inconsistent form for both Chelsea and Manchester United.

Yet he had been on Villa's list of targets - albeit a long list - while he was at Stamford Bridge as Emery was keen to sign a pacy winger in the summer.

Garnacho's problems were compounded by a head injury suffered in Thailand in pre-season, and even a boot camp during the international break in September and October, and scoring in friendlies against Sevilla and Southampton have not helped.

One of the issues Villa have is there is no exit clause, and both teams would have to agree to end the season-long loan deal early.

This time last year, Emery had already decided not to sign Harvey Elliott permanently in a Â£30m deal, leaving the on-loan Liverpool midfielder in limbo for the rest of the season.

And it appears Emery has already come to the same conclusion with Garnacho.

It has been revealed that with Villa unable to find a solution with Liverpool, Elliott wasted a precious year of his career. Those close to him recognise the damage last season did, playing just nine times after being named Player of the Tournament at the European Under-21 Championship in 2025.

He is now at Valencia and is yet to start in La Liga this season.

In a recent development, the risk of going on loan to Villa became a topic of conversation in the game because of Elliott's plight, with sources suggesting players would think twice about joining the club. Garnacho's situation only increases those concerns.

Three times in two seasons, Emery and Villa have signed a high-profile player on loan only for it to fail.

Jadon Sancho's expensive loan from Manchester United last season - Villa paying a guaranteed 80% of Sancho's wages of more than Â£200,000 a week - ended with him having made just nine Premier League starts and scoring once in 39 appearances, with 21 of those as a substitute.

Sancho may have played more than Elliott and Garnacho - and came off the bench in their Europa League final win - but what value did Villa really get?

Of course, Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio enjoyed positive loan spells previously - Rashford returning to the England squad while at Villa - but they are exceptions to the rule.

Nicolo Zaniolo, Clement Lenglet and Axel Disasi have joined in recent years and barely merit footnotes, while Douglas Luiz's loan return last season did not prompt a return to the heights he had reached previously at Villa.

The club have constantly complained about financial restrictions with some justification, but questions can certainly be asked about the money spent on many of their signings.

The blunt truth is there is no clear path.

Teenager George Hemmings has just signed a upcoming deal and has earned praise from Emery for understanding the way he wants his players to work.

Ibrahim Mbaye and Alysson are also ahead of Garnacho, leaving him well behind even before regulars John McGinn, Johan Manzambi and Emi Buendia are factored in.

There was interest from abroad in the summer, with Roma keen, and it seems increasingly unlikely we will see Garnacho at another Premier League club soon.

Fifa rules allow players to play for two clubs in a season - or three if they move to a team whose season overlaps like the MLS - meaning Garnacho could feature for another, unlike Elliott as he had already played for Liverpool and Villa.

Garnacho, whose character has not been called into question while at Villa, cost Chelsea Â£40m when he signed from Manchester United in 2025 but failed to make a consistent impression, with eight goals in 43 games. When he joined Chelsea he signed a contract until 2032.

Prior to that, United boss Ruben Amorim had told him to leave.

Now nothing, it seems, will persuade Emery that Garnacho is worth persevering with - leaving the winger's career continuing to drift.

Breaking: Stonehenge’s six-ton mystery deepens as scientists narrow their search

💡 Key Takeaways

  • A newly introduced study published in the Journal of the Geological Society presents the most comprehensive geological investigation yet of the Altar Stone, offering new clues about one of Stonehenge's most enduring mysteries.
  • Measuring 4.9 meters (about 16 feet) long, the massive sandstone slab lies at the heart of the famous prehistoric monument on Salisbury Plain in southern England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the mystery surrounding Stonehenge's enormous six-ton Altar Stone has taken another turn. Scientists have eliminated several suspected sources of the ancient sandstone slab, narrowing the search for where it originated thousands of years ago.

A newly introduced study published in the Journal of the Geological Society presents the most comprehensive geological investigation yet of the Altar Stone, offering new clues about one of Stonehenge's most enduring mysteries.

Measuring 4.9 meters (about 16 feet) long, the massive sandstone slab lies at the heart of the famous prehistoric monument on Salisbury Plain in southern England. For more than a century, archaeologists and geologists believed it had been transported from Wales. However, recent research using advanced analytical methods overturned that long-standing theory and identified northeastern Scotland as a more likely source.

Now, a upcoming international investigation has refined the search even further, although the stone's exact birthplace remains unknown.

Upcoming Geological Clues Narrow the Search.

To investigate the Altar Stone's origins, researchers combined fresh observations of the monument with detailed examinations of stone fragments preserved in museum collections.

In a recent development, using multiple scientific techniques, the team studied the sandstone's physical structure, mineral content, chemical composition, and isotopic signatures. Together, these characteristics provide a distinctive geological fingerprint that can be compared with rock formations across Britain.

The scientists focused particular attention on the Orcadian Basin in northeastern Scotland, an area previously identified as a promising candidate. However, none of the locations examined so far has produced rock with the same combination of characteristics as the Altar Stone.

Although the findings have not revealed the stone's original location, they allow researchers to eliminate several possibilities and concentrate future investigations on more promising areas.

Professor Duncan Pirrie, Emeritus Professor at the University of South Wales and leader of the study, explained:.

Sources indicate that "This is the most comprehensive geological investigation of the Altar Stone ever undertaken. By combining a wide range of analytical techniques, we have built the clearest picture yet of the stone's composition and tested the leading theories about its origins. So far, none of the locations examined have the same set of characteristics as the Altar Stone. That tells us the search is not over, but we are now far better equipped to focus on the areas most likely to yield an answer.".

From Wales to Scotland: A Century-Old Theory Overturned.

For generations, the prevailing explanation placed the Altar Stone's origins in western Wales. That assumption changed when earlier scientific investigations revealed evidence pointing much farther north, toward Scotland.

The latest findings build on that discovery by establishing more precise geological criteria for identifying a potential match.

Professor Richard Bevins, Honorary Professor in the Department of Geography and Earth Sciences at Aberystwyth University, said:.

"For almost a century, the prevailing view was that the Altar Stone came from west Wales. Our previous research overturned that assumption and pointed instead to Scotland as the most likely source. This latest study significantly refines the search by identifying the specific geological characteristics we need to look for, allowing future investigations to be targeted more effectively. With each latest piece of evidence, we move closer to solving one of Stonehenge's most enduring mysteries.".

Rather than disproving Scotland as a possible source, the new investigation helps scientists distinguish between rock formations that appear promising and those that do not match the stone's distinctive properties.

Solving Stonehenge's Six-Ton Mystery.

According to recent reports, determining where the Altar Stone came from could reveal much more than the birthplace of a single rock. It could also help explain how prehistoric communities acquired and transported enormous stones over remarkable distances.

Recent findings suggest that stonehenge was constructed in multiple stages between approximately 3000 and 1600 BC. Its builders are known to have moved massive stones across the landscape, including the smaller bluestones, which traveled roughly 225 kilometers (140 miles) from western Wales.

It has been revealed that if the Altar Stone originated in northeastern Scotland, its journey to Salisbury Plain would have been considerably longer. Establishing its precise source could therefore offer notable clues about the transportation methods, organization, and engineering abilities of the people who built Stonehenge.

Professor Nick Pearce, Emeritus Professor of Geochemistry in the Department of Geography and Earth Sciences at Aberystwyth University, emphasized why eliminating possible sources represents genuine progress:.

According to recent reports, "In a geological detective story such as this, ruling out potential source areas is just as notable as identifying upcoming ones. Every location eliminated narrows the search and brings us closer to discovering where the Altar Stone originated. The stone is unique among those at Stonehenge, and tracing its source would provide valuable new insights into its remarkable journey to Salisbury Plain thousands of years ago.".

It has been revealed that the researchers believe the detailed geological fingerprint developed during this investigation will guide future searches and could eventually identify the Altar Stone's original location. Such a discovery would help illuminate one of prehistoric Britain's most extraordinary engineering accomplishments.

The international research team included geologists and archaeologists from the United Kingdom, Canada, Italy, and Sweden. Participating organizations included the University of South Wales, Aberystwyth University, University College London, the University of Aberdeen, the University of Plymouth, the James Hutton Institute, the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, the University of Milano-Bicocca, and several industry partners.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space.

Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere.

After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets, the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were rolled out.

According to recent reports, those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space. (NASA and the U.S. military typically consider 50 miles the edge of space.) Mission control cut the flight short after about 30 seconds, because Aerobee started to yaw, and they wanted to keep it from going completely out of control.

Billed as the "most successful sounding rocket of the space age," the initial Aerobee rocket was suborbital rocket designed to launch experment payload of up to 100 pounds (45 kilograms) to an altitude of 75 miles (121 kilometers) or so.

Recent findings suggest that "The Aerobee was designed to carry instruments aloft to collect data on the upper atmosphere and to place small animals in a weightless condition for physiological studies," the U.S. National Museum of the United States Air Force wrote in a mission overview. "It was launched by a solid-propellant booster engine of 18,000 pounds thrust that burned for only two and a half seconds.".

While the first Aerobee rocket did not reach space, many more made successful releases in the decades that followed.

Recent findings suggest that engineers made a steady stream of upgrades to the the Aerobee rocket, allowing to fly higher and launch heavier payloads into space. It was an Aerobee rocket that launched two Phillipine monkeys on a mission to study how the effects of rapid launch acceleration might affect their bodies, an experiment that was among the frst human physiology tests that paved the way for human spaceflight.

More than 1,000 Aerobee rockets have introduced since then, and the last one flew in January of 1985.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, tens of thousands of flights were affected by the ground stop, which halted departing flights for more than four hours.
  • Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday that an overloaded router installed in southern Arkansas as part of an upgrade to a system overseen by L3Harris Technologies appeared to overwhelm systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Federal Aviation Administration noted Tuesday it would pause the installation of new routers after problems with the technology led the agency to matter a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday.

According to recent reports, tens of thousands of flights were affected by the ground stop, which halted departing flights for more than four hours. It was the longest halt to U.S. flight departures since 9/11.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday that an overloaded router installed in southern Arkansas as part of an upgrade to a system overseen by L3Harris Technologies appeared to overwhelm systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the news about the pause.

The FAA and Department of Transportation have said L3Harris was working to convert the communications network from copper wires to fiber optic.

Democratic members of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation this week asked the FAA and the Department of Transportation for clarity on what went wrong.

"Identifying the device that failed does not establish why it failed," the senators wrote in a statement. "Modernization cannot come at the expense of operational safety.".

The agencies have said they are working to figure out the root cause of the concern and have reiterated that there is no indication of a cyberattack or outside threat.

Sources indicate that the senators also asked for a briefing with the FAA, L3Harris and Juniper Networks, which is making the fresh devices, by Monday. They asked the companies to lay out why the operational systems lacked sufficient redundancy and answer other questions about what led to the outage.

CNBC has reached out to L3Harris and Juniper Networks for comment.

Industry observers note that duffy on Friday called for Congress to approve $50 billion in funding for upgrades to the aging U.S. air traffic control system, more than he has previously asked for. Democratic lawmakers pushed back on the request, citing unspent money from existing funding, which includes Congress' approval last year of $12.5 billion for airport and air traffic control improvements over five years.

Senate Commerce Chair Ted Cruz, R-Texas, noted Tuesday that he thinks there will be support for air traffic control modernization, but that the allocation should be specifically for safety upgrades.

Industry observers note that "I don't think the full $50 billion will be funded," he said. "Some of that is not safety related, but we just discussed there, and what I expressed is that the request needs to be focused on safety modernization.".

Sources indicate that duffy dismissed the idea that the router glitch had to do with the introduction of artificial intelligence tools and said it was "completely unfounded" because the AI system is not in communication with the defective router. He added that the FBI is helping to investigate the root cause of the issue.

Aging equipment and a shortage of air traffic controllers have for years angered airline executives, who have complained about the cost of resulting disruptions.

— CNBC's Phil LeBeau, Leslie Josephs and Justin Papp contributed to this report.

Senne Lammens (left) joined Manchester United in the summer of 2025.

After a first season at Manchester United that drew little but praise, goalkeeper Senne Lammens is under the microscope like never before.

A bad mistake that gifted Sporting their second goal on Wednesday, having earlier conceded a clumsy penalty, followed several other errors so far this season.

The 24-year-old Belgium international also made an error at the World Cup in the summer, spilling a shot that led to Spain's winning goal in the 88th minute of their quarter-final.

"I don't know [at what point Manchester United drop him]," legendary Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel told CBS Sports on Wednesday.

"Mauricio Pochettino has come in and brought his own staff. That means he's got a new goalkeeping coach and maybe that is something that can change it for him.

Recent findings suggest that "[At the World Cup] he came on against Spain and made a bit of a mistake. Mikel Merino scored and they got knocked out. I feel he's lost a little bit of confidence from that mistake and hasn't really recovered.

In a recent development, "As a goalkeeper, when you're not on your best form, you need your defenders in front of you to help you out. The sad truth is that they haven't been able to do that and that makes it so much worse. I like him a lot but today was not a great day for him.".

Three penalties and a red card as Man Utd draw against Sporting.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and United's data team overruled Ruben Amorim when they opted to sign Lammens from Royal Antwerp for Â£18.1m in September 2025.

Amorim wanted Argentina World Cup winner Emiliano Martinez, who was left waiting for a deadline day call that never came to seal a move from Aston Villa.

According to recent reports, united felt Lammens had the attributes to become one of the world's best goalkeepers. At 24, he is still young. Schmeichel was 27 when he joined United in 1991. Edwin van der Sar was 34 when he left Fulham in 2005. Both had hundreds of senior appearances behind them. Lammens has just over 100, more than half of them with Royal Antwerp.

Although he made the odd error last season, Lammens did nothing to suggest Wilcox and co had got it wrong.

After releasing Turkey international Altay Bayindir, who replaced Andre Onana as first choice at the start of last season and is back on loan in Turkey with Trabzonspor, they signed 36-year-old Wales international Karl Darlow as back-up this term.

Industry observers note that darlow finished last season as first choice at Leeds. But he only started 30 league games in three seasons with the Elland Road outfit. Also on the bench in Lisbon was Tom Heaton. The 40-year-old has not played in a senior game since February 2023.

Mistakes earlier in the season â former United midfielder Paul Scholes claimed in September '"the jury is still out" on whether Lammens is truly top class â have brought increased analysis. His positioning for Dominik Szoboszlai's opening goal for Liverpool on Sunday was questioned externally, even if United focused their attentions on Bradley Barcola shoving into the wall.

On Wednesday, it all went wrong.

Just 75 seconds after getting down to make an excellent save from Luis Suarez's first penalty, Lammens recklessly charged out and upended Maxi Araujo, even though Noussair Mazraoui seemed to be in a position to deal with it.

Then, after two Bruno Fernandes goals at the start of the second period had turned the Champions League tie in the visitors' favour, Lammens reached to collect a high ball and inexplicably dropped it in front of Suarez, who applied the overhead kick finish.

Understandably, there was sympathy in the dressing room.

"This team is a family," stated striker Joshua Zirkzee. "There's no-one who will suffer by themselves.

Recent findings suggest that "Senne is a great goalkeeper and mistakes happen. In this moment, we just give him space. I'm not sure if he wants to hear anything at all. But Senne's a great kid. He's got a good head on him. We didn't draw because of him, and we all know that next game he is going to be at the top of his game.".

'One mistake from being dropped' - Ashley Young on Senne Lammens.

Toni Jimenez is Pochettino's long-time goalkeeping coach.

His arrival triggered the exit of Craig Mawson, who had been with Manchester United since 2019. Connor King is Jimenez's assistant but a relative newcomer himself, having joined from Burnley in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that by its nature, goalkeeping at the highest level can be a mental challenge as well as a technical one. As Onana discovered, flaws can quickly become major challenges and once the spotlight is shining, the attention is fierce.

Industry observers note that lammens has given the impression privately of being strong. He has seemed remarkably unaffected by his World Cup torment â his mistake against Spain came after he was introduced as a 71st-minute replacement for injured veteran Thibaut Courtois with the quarter-final delicately poised at 1-1. But only he knows the full picture.

Jimenez will be Pochettino's guide over what to do about the situation, although for now, Lammens' head coach is behind him.

According to recent reports, "This type of thing happens," he mentioned. "That is football. Football is about making mistakes.

"I always want to support my player. I think we need to talk about responsibility. In this type of action our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult.

"It's not to blame the defensive line, but it's two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on. We need to manage his type of situation better.".

Following Wednesday's draw in Lisbon, Pochettino highlighted "two things" that need to improve if United are to start winning matches on a regular basis.

The first of those is the club's preferred goalkeeper. Of the 17 Premier League goalkeepers to have played a minimum of 10 matches in all competitions in this campaign, Lammens has the second-worst save success rate, keeping out just 60.2% of the shots he has faced. Only Coventry's Carl Rushworth (54.4%) has fared worse so far this season.

Lammens also ranks bottom of those 17 goalkeepers for clean sheet ratio (6.3%).

And there is substance to the suggestion that Lammens has declined in 2026-27. He made just one error leading to a goal in the entirety of last season in contrast to two already in this campaign. The data also shows that he is presently preventing far fewer goals.

The second "thing", however, has significant bearing on the first.

Clean sheets and conceding fewer goals are clearly a collective responsibility, particularly for the "defensive line" that Pochettino referenced on Wednesday - and United's defence has collectively struggled this season.

They have now let in 36 goals in all competitions, the most of any team in Europe's top five leagues. They have also conceded five penalties and received five red cards - both the second-highest tallies among Europe's elite divisions.

So is Lammens more error-prone this season? Apparently yes. But he's also playing behind a defence that, on current form, may not inspire too much confidence in their goalkeeper.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hair loss isn’t always dramatic. It can be incremental. You start noticing a bit more scalp in harsh bathroom lighting, a tiny bald spot when you tie your hair up in a ponytail. The shower drain is more clogged than usual. Not long ago, hair-loss treatments meant topical remedies, supplements, or a flight to Turkey. Luckily, red-light therapy brings the potential for hair regrowth into your home—no clinical appointment required.

According to recent reports, beyond skin rejuvenation, clinical studies suggest red-light therapy can help energize hair follicles, increase blood circulation in the scalp, reduce inflammation, and lower dihydrotestosterone levels—a hormone that causes hair loss and thinning. Red-light therapy also supports adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production, which helps provide oxygen and blood flow to the scalp and triggers follicles to remain in the hair growth phase.

To determine the best red-light therapy for hair growth, I tapped five WIRED tech reviewers who've dealt with hair loss themselves. We assessed red-light caps, hands-free helmets with full scalp coverage, and low-level laser therapy (LLLT) or photobiomodulation devices for 16 weeks. Along the way, I reviewed the research, spoke with dermatologists, and tracked ease of use. These are the favorites that produced meaningful results and earned our trust.

Be sure to check out our other wellness and skin-care guides, including the Best LED Masks, Best Hair Dryers, and Best Blow Dry Brushes.

Recent findings suggest that love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.

Updated November 2026: I added the Capillus HairBand to Honorable Mentions, and I included a product to avoid. Prices, links, and product information were also updated.

Sources indicate that to start, I consulted board-certified dermatologists and referred to clinical trials to help determine what features to look for when shopping for a device. I test these devices with several tech reviewers on our team, all of whom have personal experience with hair thinning or loss to different degrees. Most of these at-home gadgets call for a 16-week treatment cycle. We follow the brands' directions and record any visible results along the way.

Sources indicate that we monitor changes in hair count, hair density, and scalp health, but effectiveness is only one of the factors we consider. We also judge ease of use, functionality, and comfort. We note the specific wavelengths of light and whether the treatment options feel tolerable or difficult to integrate into everyday routines.

According to recent reports, we also prioritize safety, checking for FDA clearance, automatic shut-off features, and overall durability of the design. To date, our testers have not experienced any side effects, but we would have documented them had they.

Feels a little pointless to look outdoor-ready when you can’t actually use it on the go. It also got too hot for me to wear comfortably. —Nena Farrell.

Does Red-Light Therapy Work for Hair Loss?

Yes—research suggests low-level light therapy can work for certain types of hair loss, such as androgenetic alopecia, also known as male or female pattern hair loss. It can help increase hair count, thickness, and density by stimulating hair follicles and boosting cellular activity in the scalp.

That said, results depend heavily on the type and severity of hair loss. Red-light therapy works best in cases of mild to moderate thinning and may be less effective for advanced hair loss or scarring conditions like cicatricial alopecia. Consistency also matters. You typically need regular, ongoing use to maintain results, and benefits can diminish if treatments stop.

What Wavelength of Red Light Is Best for Hair Restoration?

Recent findings suggest that according to the American Hair Loss Association, wavelengths in the range of 630 to 680 nanometers are ideal for hair regrowth. These wavelengths are known to support increased blood flow to the scalp, boost cellular activity, and help reduce inflammation. Some clinical studies specifically cite 650 nanometers as an especially effective wavelength.

Sources indicate that red-light devices that use medical-grade laser diodes tend to deliver more targeted and consistent light than standard LEDs, but both can stimulate hair follicles at the right wavelengths. For best results, look for FDA-cleared devices that list their wavelengths and power output.

How to Use Red-Light Therapy for Hair Growth.

Consistency is the most important part of any red-light therapy routine. Most devices require at least three months of use before noticeable results are observed, and some may take longer. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions, as treatment schedules vary by device, but most recommend sessions three to five times per week. The hair growth is preserved only with continued use, so you’ll need ongoing maintenance sessions.

Always start with a clean and dry scalp so the light can reach your hair follicles without interference from oils or styling products. Some devices include protective eyewear, and if yours does, wear it during treatment. Make sure to wipe the device down with a gentle disinfectant before or after each session to prevent buildup on the LEDs.

Topical regrowth treatments can complement red-light therapy and may help support thicker hair. A few randomized clinical trials suggest that combining minoxidil (2 percent or 5 percent) with red-light therapy can improve hair density and encourage faster regrowth compared to using either treatment alone. For a natural alternative, some research has found rosemary oil to produce results comparable to 2 percent minoxidil for androgenetic alopecia, though the evidence isn’t as extensive as it is for minoxidil.

If you’re pregnant or have an underlying medical condition, talk to your healthcare provider before starting any form of red-light therapy.

Is Red-Light Therapy for Hair Growth Safe?

Yes—for most people, red-light therapy is considered a safe and noninvasive treatment with minimal side effects when used as intended. Still, it's always worth consulting a health care professional before starting any sort of treatment. This is especially the case for anyone with photosensitive conditions or autoimmune disorders that affect light sensitivity.

Sources indicate that I prefer devices that are FDA-cleared because it means they've met certain safety standards for consumer use. But keep in mind that the clearance process is less rigorous than the FDA approval pathway, as it just requires manufacturers to prove their product is “substantially equivalent” to an already legally marketed device. Also, FDA clearance isn't a guarantee of results; it simply means it's considered safe to use as directed at home.

Bizarre deep-sea fish with a see-through head captured in stunning 4K

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A rare encounter nearly 2,000 feet beneath the ocean's surface gave scientists an extraordinary opportunity to film one of the deep sea's most unusual creatures.
  • According to recent reports, the discovery occurred during an expedition aboard the research vessel David Packard.
  • In a recent development, members of MBARI's Biodiversity and Biooptics Team were investigating marine life approximately 90 kilometers (55 miles) offshore when they spotted the fish about 600 meters (1,970 feet) below the surface.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A rare encounter nearly 2,000 feet beneath the ocean's surface gave scientists an extraordinary opportunity to film one of the deep sea's most unusual creatures. Researchers from the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute (MBARI) spotted a barreleye fish (Macropinna microstoma), a mysterious species known for its transparent head and remarkable eyes that can rotate to track prey.

According to recent reports, the discovery occurred during an expedition aboard the research vessel David Packard. It marked only the eleventh time MBARI scientists have encountered this elusive fish during nearly four decades of ocean exploration.

In a recent development, members of MBARI's Biodiversity and Biooptics Team were investigating marine life approximately 90 kilometers (55 miles) offshore when they spotted the fish about 600 meters (1,970 feet) below the surface. Using the remotely operated vehicle (ROV) Doc Ricketts, the researchers were filming and collecting deep-sea organisms when the unexpected visitor appeared.

In a recent development, "Seeing a barreleye fish is a rare treat. Crew from across the ship joined the science team in the control room, mesmerized by this remarkable animal. Deep-sea animals capture the imagination, creating wonder and awe that we hope will inspire stewardship of the largest living space on Earth," said Senior Scientist Steven Haddock.

[See video link after end of article.].

A Surprise Encounter Deep in the Pacific Ocean.

Recent findings suggest that the discovery was an unexpected highlight of the eight-day Diving Deep for Delicate Drifters expedition. Haddock and his colleagues had primarily been investigating gelatinous marine animals, including jellyfish, siphonophores, and ctenophores, also known as comb jellies. Their research seeks to understand how these delicate organisms have evolved to survive in the open ocean at great depths.

Industry observers note that to investigate life throughout the water column, the team combined blue-water scuba dives near the surface with remotely operated vehicle surveys hundreds of meters below. These complementary approaches allowed researchers to observe and collect animals living in very different parts of the ocean.

The barreleye appeared just as the day's underwater operations were coming to an end. The ROV pilots were "flying" Doc Ricketts toward the surface for recovery when Research Specialist Shannon Johnson noticed the unusual fish and immediately asked them to stop.

Sources indicate that most of the scientists had already moved to the ship's wet lab, where they were preparing to catalog specimens collected during the dive. When word spread about the sighting, they hurried back to the control room, accompanied by crew members eager to see the extraordinary animal. The rare encounter provided an exciting conclusion to a busy and productive week of exploration.

How the Barreleye Fish Uses Its Transparent Head to Hunt.

Recent findings suggest that the barreleye's strange appearance is more than a biological curiosity. Its unusual anatomy helps it find food in the ocean's twilight zone, a dimly lit region where sunlight is faint and spotting prey can be difficult.

Earlier observations by MBARI Senior Scientist Bruce Robison and Research Specialist Kim Reisenbichler helped scientists understand how this remarkable fish hunts.

Rather than constantly swimming in search of food, Macropinna can remain nearly motionless in the water, supported by its large fins, which provide both stability and precise control over its movements. Its tubular eyes normally point upward, allowing it to watch for the faint silhouettes of animals passing overhead.

According to recent reports, once the fish detects something worth eating, its eyes can rotate within a transparent dome of tissue covering the top of its head. This unusual ability allows the barreleye to maintain visual contact with prey as it changes position to capture it.

The clear, gelatinous covering serves another important purpose. Barreleyes can feed on small crustaceans trapped among the stinging tentacles of deep-sea siphonophores, which are colonial animals related to jellyfish. The protective dome helps shield the fish's sensitive eyes while it retrieves its meal.

Rare 4K Footage Reveals Extraordinary Details.

According to recent reports, scientists were able to spend approximately 20 minutes watching the barreleye during the encounter. Using the high-resolution 4K camera aboard Doc Ricketts, they recorded unusually detailed views of its anatomy and movements.

In a recent development, the team also adjusted the vehicle's lighting to make the fish's transparent head shield easier to observe. These changes helped reveal the unusual structures that make this species so distinctive.

In a recent development, ROV Pilot/Technician Cameron Law brought Doc Ricketts close enough to capture additional footage with the vehicle's virtual reality camera. The resulting 3D stereo imagery provides another perspective on the fish and could eventually be used in educational programs and public outreach.

It has been revealed that "Macropinna reminds us of the surprising ways that animals have adapted to thrive in the ocean's midwater," noted Haddock. "So many of them survive by looking for subtle optical cues, like a shadow passing overhead, and this sets off evolutionary competition, pitting bioluminescent camouflage against increasingly sophisticated visual capabilities.".

An Extraordinary Sighting After Nearly 7,000 Deep-Sea Dives.

The rarity of the encounter becomes even more striking when considering MBARI's extensive exploration history. Over nearly 40 years, the institute has conducted approximately 7,000 remotely operated vehicle dives and accumulated more than 41,000 hours of deep-sea video. Despite that enormous effort, researchers have recorded just 11 encounters with Macropinna microstoma.

MBARI's previous sighting of Macropinna occurred in 2021. The latest encounter represents two vital firsts for the institute: its first 4K footage of this species and its first observation of the fish from the newly introduced flagship research vessel David Packard.

MBARI scientists have also encountered other members of the barreleye family during their ocean expeditions. This summer, researchers working with Schmidt Ocean Institute in the mid-Atlantic Ocean recorded another unusual deep-sea species, the binocular fish (Winteria telescopa).

Together, these encounters provide rare opportunities to observe the remarkable adaptations that allow animals to survive far beneath the ocean's surface, where light is scarce and much of the marine environment remains unexplored.

The Diving Deep for Delicate Drifters expedition was supported through the David and Lucile Packard Foundation's longstanding commitment to MBARI's scientific research.

What OPEC's surprise oil cut means for gas prices

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • OPEC and its allies’ surprise move to slash oil production will soon be felt at US gas pumps.
  • The group known as OPEC+ confirmed Sunday it would cut oil production by more than 1.6 million barrels a day starting in May, running through the end of the year.
  • The production cut announcement also had an immediate impact on gasoline futures, which will be passed onto US drivers much more quickly than the spike in oil prices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

OPEC and its allies’ surprise move to slash oil production will soon be felt at US gas pumps.

The group known as OPEC+ confirmed Sunday it would cut oil production by more than 1.6 million barrels a day starting in May, running through the end of the year. The news sent both Brent crude futures, the global oil benchmark, and WTI, the US benchmark, up about 6% in trading Monday.

The production cut announcement also had an immediate impact on gasoline futures, which will be passed onto US drivers much more quickly than the spike in oil prices. RBOB, the most closely watched wholesale gasoline price, was up about 8 cents a gallon, or about 3%, in morning trading.

“I think OPEC is reawakening the inflation monster,” said Tom Kloza, global head of energy analysis for OPIS, which tracks gas prices for AAA. “The White House has to be shocked and major-time pissed. It certainly alters the calculus for a while.”.

In a recent development, the national average for US gas prices stood at $3.51, on Monday, according to AAA. Kloza stated he could see it getting up to $3.80 to $3.90 in relatively short order thanks to the move by OPEC.

Industry observers note that “We’re not going to get back to $5 a gallon. I don’t think we’re even going as high as $4,” he said. But he said by the end of the summer US drivers could be back above year-earlier prices, especially if there is a hurricane or other storms affecting production along the Gulf Coast.

It has been revealed that the average US regular gas price a year ago stood at $4.19 a gallon in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the disruption that caused to world’s energy markets. Prices eventually reached a record $5.02 a gallon on June 14, before starting a slow but steady decline over the course of more than three months during which the average price fell every day. The decline was partly driven by the release of oil from the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve, and partly by concerns that there could be a US or global recession that reduced the demand for gasoline.

Oil prices surge after OPEC+ producers announce surprise cuts.

Sources indicate that even at $3.51, US gas prices were just below the $3.53 average on Feb. 23, 2022, the day before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

In a recent development, kloza said one thing keeping prices from getting anywhere near the record levels of 2022 is that the US prepares additional releases from the SPR, and US oil production and refining capacity are both up. But a cut of 1 million barrels a day of oil by OPEC+ will not be easy to make up.

“They have ability to cut production and they seem motivated to do so,” he said.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Long-held assumptions are beginning to crumble, including the belief that the US would ultimately remain firmly on Germany's side.
  • In a recent development, in the foundation's latest poll on public attitudes on German foreign policy, 65% of respondents noted they fear further military conflicts around the world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for decades, German foreign policy was never seen as particularly controversial at home. The country was firmly integrated into NATO and supported EU expansion and cooperation across Europe. It also advocated for multilateral approaches to resolving conflicts around the world. All of this enjoyed broad public support. But all of this has also changed since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the wars in the Middle East. Now, Germany's foreign policy has become increasingly contentious and is fueling growing public anxiety.

Long-held assumptions are beginning to crumble, including the belief that the US would ultimately remain firmly on Germany's side. This is one of the central findings of a new survey by the Hamburg-based Körber Foundation.

In a recent development, in the foundation's latest poll on public attitudes on German foreign policy, 65% of respondents noted they fear further military conflicts around the world. Meanwhile, 48% believe that Germany should adopt a more restrained approach to international affairs — a five percentage point increase from last year.

Since 2017, the non-profit Körber Foundation, established in the northern German city of Hamburg in 1959 by industrialist Kurt Körber, has conducted the annual surveys titled "the Berlin Pulse." For this year's study, the polling institute Forsa surveyed around 1,500 eligible voters in September.

The findings make one thing clear: The current government's approach under Chancellor Friedrich Merz — seeking to have a say in virtually every international conflict and drawing on Germany's position as the largest EU economy — is increasingly met with skepticism. Only 40% of respondents now favor greater international engagement, down from 48% in 2025.

Florian Bigge, who helped compile the study for the Körber Foundation, commented on the findings on Monday: "This is a significant decline, especially since we have been asking this question for years, with changes in the range of just two to three percentage points.".

Meanwhile, 77% of respondents want Germany to focus primarily on diplomacy rather than military action.

Industry observers note that the most dramatic shift in public opinion concerns the war in Ukraine. Germany's military support for the Eastern European country, including the delivery of billions of euros' worth of weapons, no longer has the backing of a majority of the population. In September 2026, only 46% of respondents supported continued military assistance, compared to 59% in the previous year's survey. Right now, a narrow majority of 53% want to halt weapons deliveries altogether.

As Jonathan Lehrer of "the Berlin Pulse" explains, opposition is particularly strong among supporters of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD).

Industry observers note that "Eighty-eight precent of AfD supporters oppose military assistance to Ukraine," Lehrer noted. "This is an interesting finding, especially considering political developments in Germany, including state elections in which the AfD gained support by campaigning against aid to Ukraine.".

The AfD has recently overtaken the chancellor's conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) in nationwide polls.

Support for Ukraine was also the subject of a recent poll conducted by the opinion research institute Infratest Dimap. This study also found that public support for Ukraine is continuing to decline, with a majority now opposed to providing assistance (see graphic).

One finding from the Berlin Pulse study is particularly alarming for politicians and experts committed to transatlantic relations. As the US and China are increasingly seen as rivals on the global stage, 83% of respondents believe that Germany should remain neutral. Only 15% would side with the US.

This may stem from the policies of US President Donald Trump. Florian Bigge of the Körber Foundation stated of the widespread preference for neutrality: "This sentiment is strong among Germans across all age groups and political parties. In eastern Germany, support for neutrality is at 92%, compared to 81% in the west. We interpret this as a desire for security but also reluctant commitment: Germans do not want to take sides in this conflict between the great powers.".

The picture becomes clearer when respondents are asked about Russia. Under President Vladimir Putin, 82% of those surveyed see Russia as a military threat. However, public opinion is more divided when Germany responds firmly to such threats, including hybrid attacks. For instance, after the attempted drone attack on Leipzig Airport in early May, Germany responded by closing the Russian consulate in Bonn. However, only 51% support such measures, while 46% favor a more restrained approach.

"The gap between external expectations and domestic support is the central challenge facing German foreign policy," noted Sarah Pagung of the Körber Foundation.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

One issue that appears to cause relatively little concern among Germans is the conflict in the Middle East, despite the devastating situation in the Gaza Strip following Hamas's terrorist attack on Israel more than three years ago.

This may also have to do with changing public attitudes toward Israel. One question in the study asked: "Does Germany have a special historical and moral responsibility for Israel's security because of the Holocaust?".

Sources indicate that the results were striking: 61% of respondents noted no, while just 36% answered yes. Among those under 25, opposition to Germany's special responsibility toward the Jewish state was even higher, at 75%.

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bella Hadid is sharing latest revelations about her health.

The 30-year-old explained how managing several medical conditions in addition to Lyme disease—which her mom, Yolanda Hadid, first shared her daughter had in 2015—impacts her, explaining, "My body just can’t connect with my brain.".

"I have POTS, and I have a lot of PMDD, endometriosis," Bella told Harper's Bazaar in an interview published Nov. 23. "Plus my Lyme and things that affect my body very deeply.".

While premenstrual dysphoric disorder and endometriosis are illnesses related to the female reproductive system that cause painful and exhausting menstrual cycles, according to the Cleveland Clinic, postural orthostatic tachycardia is a syndrome that causes a person's heart to beat faster when they change the position of their body.

And in speaking about her diagnoses, the Beauty actress was brought back to a time when a frightening flare-up threatened to keep her off the runway.

Recent findings suggest that "Right before I walked out on the runway for my opening look, I went to go stretch and my whole clavicle completely—," she recounted. "I don’t even know what it was. My lungs almost collapsed, and I couldn’t breathe.".

And with her following the family business in fashion along with Yolanda's other two kids, Gigi Hadid, 31, and Anwar Hadid, 27, Bella admitted the painful interruptions shake her confidence to perform.

"My body goes through these different motions of feeling really good and then all of a sudden crashing on me at the worst moments," she continued. "Because I know how to walk. One thing I can do is I can strut. But it’s a lot of pressure; we all have our own insecurities.".

With that in mind, the Victoria's Secret Angel has to remind herself, "maybe my body can’t handle all that I have going on," which ultimately results in the freedom to decide, "'No, we can’t do that today.'".

Earlier this year, the model—who recently went public with her relationship with boyfriend Nathan Lacy—explained how her health struggles can feel isolating.

"Sometimes it feels like unless you've lived something like this, or loved someone who has," Bella captioned a June 26 Instagram Story, "it's impossible to understand.".

Read on for more stars who have walked the world through their health challenges.

Travis Barker's Precancer Diagnosis.

The Blink-182 drummer stopped smoking weed after being diagnosed with "precancer of the esophagus.".

"I loved blunts and I would smoke too much," he shared on a November 2026 episode of the Big Bro with Kid Cudi podcast, recalling how his doctor stated it was a "serious case. "He’s like, ‘This is your warning shot. Don’t f--l around. You’ve got to stop smoking.".

The Jessie alum opened up about her "hellish" migraines, sharing how they've worsened after suffering five concussions over the course of her life.

Industry observers note that "The brain injuries make things significantly worse," Ryan shared during a September 2026 episode of Mythical Kitchen’s Last Meals. "I had a pretty crazy, life-altering brain injury a few years ago, and I was out of commission for six months.".

While Ryan described her first four concussions as "incidents," she said her fifth one was trauma caused by "sustained shaking over a minute of time.".

Now, the former Disney Channel star needs to close her eyes to "think better.".

"Quite often the world is really loud. It’s really too bright. There’s a lot going on," she explained. "The visual data that I'm taking in can be so distracting and so loud. Then, with the migraines—which are significantly worsened by that—it sort of is too much.".

Brianna "Chickenfry" LaPaglia's Ovarian Cyst.

In May 2026, the BFFs podcaster underwent emergency surgery after doctors discovered a large ovarian cyst that had been twisting her organs and causing internal bleeding.

"There was a half a liter of blood in my pelvic floor," Brianna shared in a TikTok video after the operation. "I have five incisions all over my stomach. They went in through my belly button with a camera so they could find all the blood.".

Nikki Garcia's Breast Implant Injury.

The Total Bellas alum revealed that one of her breast implants shifted after an elbow slam from fellow WWE star Piper Niven during a July 2025 wrestling match.

In a recent development, "It's OK," she told sister Bella Garcia at the time. "We're going to get it fixed one day. I told the doctor, I go, 'Newly divorced, so the minute the boots are hung up, I'm going to come back to you and we're going to make these girls look real good, because these girls are going to get some action in the future and that can't look like that.'".

In October 2026, the former The Bachelorette star detailed how she cracked a vertebra in her spine after setting her vibration plate—a motorized platform that rapidly moves back and forth to promote muscle activation and circulation—to "level 30, supersonic speed.".

"Seemingly, subtly, somewhere on the way to 30, maybe 10 or 20, my vertebrae turn crooked and rub against each other," Windey shared in a Substack essaye aptly titled "Broke back, no mountain.".

It has been revealed that "It was too fast vibrations I guess, and too many vibrations maybe, and too much pressure to shake," she continued. "And it broke. Broke right off, like your ex-boyfriend’s bumper. Well, technically, it cracked.".

The injury left her with what she described as "insatiable" paresthesia—a medical term for a tingling, pins-and-needles sensation.

Industry observers note that "This is the greatest sense of condemnation; of persecution, I’ll ever feel," she added. "And I do wish it on my worst enemy If only they hadn’t wished it on me first.".

Lupita Nyong'o's Uterine Fibroids.

The 12 Years a Slave star was diagnosed with uterine fibroids—non-cancerous growths that develop in or around the uterus—in 2014, the same year she won an Oscar for performance in the movie.

However, it wasn't until 2025 when she disclosed her diagnosis, writing on Instagram that she had been "suffering in silence" for more than a decade.

Recent findings suggest that "When we reach puberty, we're taught periods mean pain, and that pain is simply part of being a woman," she shared. "We're struggling alone with something that affects us most.".

Brian Austin Green's Perforated Appendix.

The Beverly Hills, 90210 alum revealed in April 2025 that he was recovering from surgery after his appendix nearly burst.

“Last week, I started feeling some pain in my stomach,” Brian noted in an Instagram video at the time. “I ended up going to the emergency room, and I had a perforated appendix. Not quite burst, but just before.”.

He added, “I'm on the road to recovery. It's not an easy process. This is my first major surgery.”.

In July 2025, the Daisy Jones & The Six star shared that she had been hospitalized due to a hernia—a gap in the muscular wall that's commonly found in the abdomen or groin area—caused by wearing tight pants.

It has been revealed that "'Suki you never tweet anymore,'" she wrote on X, formerly known as Twitter. "Have you ever considered I wore pants so tight 6 months ago it caused a hernia & I’ve been too scared to tell you?".

Savannah DeMelo's Mid-Game "Medical Emergency" Mid-Game.

The Racing Louisville midfielder collapsed just a few minutes into her soccer team's September 2025 match against Seattle Reign at Lumen Field in Seatle.

The United States Women’s National Team player could be seen slowly sitting down on the field with a teammate by her side, per Reuters, as the referee called for trainers to check her out. She collapsed seconds later.

“Savannah received immediate on-field care from medical personnel and was transported to a local hospital for further evaluation,” the National Women’s Soccer League wrote on X later that night. “She is stable and alert.".

Adam Devine's Long-Term Injury From Childhood Accident.

Adam Devine shared that injuries he sustained after getting hit by a cement truck when he was 11 years old are still affecting him to this day.

“It’s been a nightmare,” Devine noted in a 2025 episode of the In Depth With Graham Bensinger podcast. “I have spasms all over. For a while, [the doctors] told me I was dying—literally, within this last year.”.

He noted that pain comes and goes, adding, "My body has all these things that are a little wonky and a little wrong with it.".

The Bachelor Nation alum shared that he went to the hospital “crawling on all fours” due to overwhelming back pain that was aggravated during an RV trip with a friend.

Recent findings suggest that “Right now, knees to my toes, it’s, like, still tingly, which is crazy,” he said on a March 2025 episode of his Trading Secrets podcast. “And to put in perspective, I don’t know, man, like not to sound douchey, but like two, three weeks ago, maybe a month ago, I was squatting probably like 295 pounds. And right now, I can’t do a squat on my foot. I can’t do a one legged squat, I fall. It’s like I had a stroke or something.”.

But with the help of a back specialist and some steroids, he added, “We’re on the mend.”.

Matt Kirschenheiter's Heart Attack.

Real Housewives of Orange County’s Gina Kirschenheiter shared her ex-husband Matt Kirschenheiter suffered a heart attack in March 2025, but thankfully survived the ordeal.

Tracy Morgan's Medical Emergency.

The 30 Rock star suffered a health scare at a New York Knicks basketball game in March 2025, leading to him being wheeled out of Madison Square Garden.

However, the comedian shared an revision on social media the following day, noting it was a case of food poisoning and that he was on the mend.

Christy Carlson Romano's Eye Injury.

The Even Stevens alum shared in February 2025 that she was shot in the face while on a trip to shoot clay pigeons to celebrate husband Brendan Rooney's birthday.

Recent findings suggest that "There was another party with us and they unsafely fired in the wrong direction and shot me in the face," she wrote on Instagram. "@thebrendanrooney immediately sprung into action, assessed me, and rushed me to the hospital. I was hit in 5 places, one was less than an inch from hitting me directly in my right eye.".

The Kim Possible alum continued, "Unfortunately a fragment got lodged behind my eye and it is too risky to remove surgically at this time. Doctors will continue to monitor me (I can see normally at the moment).".

Sources indicate that the actress remarked she was grateful to be alive. "I love my daughters, husband, family, and friends so much," she said. "I saw my life flash before my eyes and I’m telling you, hug the people around you every chance you can. Life can change in an instant.".

Industry observers note that while the internet isn't always a kind place, Amy Schumer is happy that, in this case, it helped her get answers."The internet really came for me after doing a bunch of press, and I was like, 'OK everybody, relax,'" Amy recalled of her "puffier" face on a January 2025 episode of Call Her Daddy. "But then doctors were chiming in in the comments and they were like, 'No no, we think something’s really up. Your face looks so crazy that we think something’s up. And I’m like, ‘Wait, I’m getting trolled by doctors?’"After these doctors remarked they thought she had Cushing syndrome and that it may be caused by spiking coritsol levels or steroid injections, the Life & Beth creator thought, "Wait, I have been getting steroid injections in my scars.""I had a breast reduction, a C-section, whatever, and so I was getting these steroid injections," Amy said. "So it gave me this thing called Cushing syndrome, which I wouldn’t have known if the internet hadn’t come for me so hard."Toda, Amy is just relieved she's OK. As she shared in a February 2024 News Not Noise newsletter, "Finding out I have the kind of Cushing that will just work itself out and I'm healthy was the greatest news imaginable.".

Casey Fitzgerald's Neck Injury From Hockey Skate Blade.

Recent findings suggest that the AHL player was cut by a fellow player's skate during a game in December 2024 and received 25 stitches. His father, Fresh Jersey Devils general manager Tom Fitzgerald later told ESPN after his son was fully recovered, "We're very lucky. I don't wish that on any parent.".

Recent findings suggest that hailey Bieber had the "scariest moment" of her life when she was having breakfast with husband Justin Bieber and started experiencing stroke-like symptoms in March 2022."Justin was like, 'Are you OK?'" the Rhode skincare mogul shared a month later on YouTube, "and I just didn't respond because I wasn't sure. And then he asked me again and when I went to respond, I couldn't speak. The right side of my face started drooping. I couldn't get a sentence out."While Hailey said the facial drooping stopped and her speech came back, she went to the hospital to make sure she was OK."They did some scans and they were able to see that I had suffered a small blood clot to my brain," the model added, "which they labeled and categorized as something called a TIA [Transient Ischemic Attack]."Later, Hailey went to the University of California, Los Angeles, where she found out she had a hole in her heart called a patent foramen ovale (PFO).She explained the blood clot had traveled into her heart, "escaped" through the hole and went to her brain, leading to the TIA.Hailey said she had a successful PFO closure procedure and was now feeling great.

Justin Bieber's Ramsay Hunt Syndrome.

According to recent reports, the same year Hailey had her health scare, Justin experienced one of his own.In June 2022, the "Baby" singer shared he was diagnosed with Ramsay Hunt syndrome, a condition that caused temporary paralysis to parts of his face and forced him to cancel the remainder of his Justice World Tour."It is from this virus that attacks the nerve in my ear and my facial nerves and has caused my face to have paralysis," Justin explained in an Instagram video at the time. "As you can see, this eye is not blinking. I can't smile on this side of my face. This nostril will not move. So, there's full paralysis on this side of my face."In fact, he told his followers it had gotten "progressively harder to eat." But after a while, the paralysis went away."He's doing really well," Hailey mentioned on a June 2022 episode of Good Morning America, later adding, "He's feeling a lot better. Obviously, it was just a very scary and random situation to happen, but he's going to be totally OK and I'm just grateful that he's fine.".

Jamie Foxx's Brain Bleed & Stroke.

While Jamie Foxx initially kept details of his April 2023 hospitalization private, he later opened up about what he went through.One day in Atlanta, "I was having such a bad headache, so I asked my boy, I stated, ‘Listen, I need an aspirin,’” the Oscar winner said in his 2024 Netflix special What Had Happened Was... “Before I could get the Aspirin, I went out. I don’t remember 20 days.”Jamie said he was initially taken to a doctor who gave him a cortisone shot and then sent him home. However, his concerned sister Deidra Dixon then drove him to a hospital, where they got an answer: He had a brain bleed that led to a stroke.Twenty days after undergoing an operation, the Django Unchained woke up May 4 in a wheelchair and couldn’t walk. He then went to Chicago for rehabilitation and therapy."All I can tell you is that I appreciate every prayer,” he said, “because I needed every prayer.”.

Tracey Yukich's Medical Emergency on The Biggest Loser.

The reality star revealed that she "died" while running a mile during the first challenge of the NBC competition series.

“I don't remember a lot,” she explained on Fit for TV: The Reality of The Biggest Loser. “I remember hearing the helicopter. I just felt like I was floating. And then my grandpa was there. And then I saw darkness. But then I saw light. So I knew, I knew I died that day.”.

“My organs were literally shutting down,” she continued. “I didn't realize that I had rhabdomyolysis. And rhabdomyolysis is your body's way of saying, ‘I'm going to shut down on you.’”.

Emilia Clarke filmed battle scenes for Game of Thrones, but in 2019, she published an essay in The New Yorker titled "A Battle for My Life."Having a bad headache at the gym, "I reached the toilet, sank to my knees, and proceeded to be violently, voluminously ill," the actress wrote. "Meanwhile, the pain—shooting, stabbing, constricting pain—was getting worse. At some level, I knew what was happening: my brain was damaged."She was taken to the hospital for a brain scan."The diagnosis was quick and ominous: a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), a life-threatening type of stroke, caused by bleeding into the space surrounding the brain," the Emmy nominee added. "I’d had an aneurysm, an arterial rupture."Emilia had immediate surgery to seal the aneurysm, calling the pain "unbearable." While she was recovering, she continued, she experienced aphasia and was "muttering nonsense."A week later, "the aphasia passed," Emilia added, and she left the hospital a month after being admitted. At a 2013 brain scan, she learned a growth "doubled in size" and that she needed surgery again."When they woke me, I was screaming in pain," she wrote. "The procedure had failed. I had a massive bleed and the doctors made it plain that my chances of surviving were precarious if they didn’t operate again. This time they needed to access my brain in the old-fashioned way—through my skull."Thankfully, Emilia shared, she's now "at a hundred per cent.".

Snoop Dogg's daughter Cori Broadus is grateful for her family.Because after she suffered a "severe stroke" in January 2024, her loved ones rushed to be by her side."I texted them that I just had a stroke and sent them a picture," she told E! News correspondent Will Marfuggi in December 2024. "Everybody just came to my rescue."Because of other medical concerns, Cori ended up staying in the hospital longer than she initially expected."I could have went home after my stroke, but my lupus wasn't doing so well," the Snoop's Fatherhood: Cori and Wayne's Story star continued. "My kidneys were failing. It was a lot going on."Today, Cori is on the mend."I'm doing great," she added. "I just had a little bit of motor skills that I had to work back on. But other than that, I was fine.".

Shailene Woodley's Health Battle.

Shailene Woodley’s early 20s were not an easy time health-wise.“It got to the point where I was losing my hearing. I couldn’t walk for longer than five minutes at a time without having to lay down for hours, and hours and sleep. Everything I ate hurt my stomach,” the actress said on a September 2024 episode of the SHE MD Podcast. “It was this conflation of complications and diagnoses and different doctors telling me different things.”So Shailene—who chose to keep the exact condition private—set out to find answers. “I come from a very holistic background and study herbalism,” she added. “So I was very keen on, ‘I’m going to work with real MDs, [and] I’m also going to work with independent kind of healers.’ Just trying to search for some sense of comfort in my own skin.”It was a long journey—one that lasted for 10 years.“Throughout that decade, a lot of other things came from feeling so much discomfort physically,” the Big Little Lies star noted, “which was, ‘My gosh, if everything I eat hurts my stomach, I’m now suddenly afraid of food.’ And then going into the kind of mental f--ckery that can happen with that of body dysmorphia and confusion about identity and feeling safe in my own capsule, in my own skin, what that meant, and what that should be.”After tending to both her physical and mental health, Shailene is feeling much better.“It was a journey that ultimately physically resolved itself, and I am very healthy,” she shared. “I’m so happy to be able to say that.".

#196680. Breaking: Too much exercise could leave your brain stuck in overdrive

Breaking: Too much exercise could leave your brain stuck in overdrive

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1148 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that exercising too intensely without enough recovery time may affect more than muscles and physical endurance.
  • In a fresh study published in the journal Neuroscience, researchers in Brazil found that prolonged, exhausting exercise altered dopamine regulation in the hippocampus, a brain region notable for memory and emotional regulation.
  • According to recent reports, the scientists observed that mice exposed to demanding exercise schedules continued to have elevated dopamine levels during periods when they should have been recovering.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that exercising too intensely without enough recovery time may affect more than muscles and physical endurance. New research suggests that excessive training can also disrupt brain chemistry, potentially interfering with the processes that help the brain return to its normal resting state.

In a fresh study published in the journal Neuroscience, researchers in Brazil found that prolonged, exhausting exercise altered dopamine regulation in the hippocampus, a brain region notable for memory and emotional regulation.

According to recent reports, the scientists observed that mice exposed to demanding exercise schedules continued to have elevated dopamine levels during periods when they should have been recovering. Dopamine plays an notable role in motivation and alertness, and the researchers believe that similar disruptions in humans could help explain why excessive training is sometimes associated with insomnia, anxiety, and persistent fatigue. If confirmed, this connection would provide further evidence that sufficient rest is essential for both physical fitness and mental well-being.

"Our findings show that excessive physical exercise affects not only skeletal muscle but also has a pronounced impact on the brain," remarked Alisson Luiz da Rocha, the study's first author.

Industry observers note that rocha carried out the research during his doctoral studies at the Ribeirão Preto School of Physical Education and Sports at the University of São Paulo (EEFERP-USP) in Brazil, supported by a scholarship from FAPESP. He explained that the findings demonstrate how exercise influences the central nervous system, with effects extending well beyond muscle development.

How Scientists Simulated Overtraining.

To investigate what happens in the brain when exercise becomes excessive, the team studied two main groups of mice exposed to different levels of physical activity.

One group completed a single strenuous treadmill session, running until they reached exhaustion. The other followed an extended training program designed to reproduce the demanding conditions associated with overtraining syndrome in elite athletes.

It has been revealed that overtraining syndrome occurs when the physical demands of training exceed the body's ability to recover. It can cause declining athletic performance, reduced appetite, ongoing fatigue, muscle pain, and a greater risk of injuries. Changes in immune function and metabolism are also common.

In a recent development, for the extended training experiment, the mice exercised over eight weeks as the researchers gradually increased the workload. By the final week, they were completing two sessions each day, with only four hours of recovery between workouts.

Industry observers note that after the exercise programs, the scientists examined the animals' hippocampi. They measured dopamine and serotonin, along with proteins involved in producing and managing these chemical messengers. These included tyrosine hydroxylase (TyrH), an enzyme needed for dopamine production, and vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2), which helps package neurotransmitters for release.

Dopamine Remained Elevated for 48 Hours.

In mice that completed just one exhausting treadmill session, dopamine levels increased shortly after exercise. This demonstrated that even a single bout of intense activity could produce a measurable chemical response in the brain.

Recent findings suggest that the more striking results came from the animals that underwent weeks of demanding training. In this group, both dopamine and TyrH remained elevated for 48 hours after the performance test, even though the mice were in their recovery period.

This prolonged response suggests that repeated strenuous exercise without sufficient rest may interfere with the brain's normal regulation of dopamine. Rather than quickly returning to its usual chemical state, the brain continued to show signs of altered neurotransmitter activity long after the exercise had ended.

Adelino Sanchez Ramos da Silva, a professor at EEFERP-USP who coordinated the study, explained that finding comparable changes in humans could help researchers better understand the possible connections between overtraining, brain chemistry, and sleep disturbances.

However, the researchers caution that the study did not directly measure sleep, anxiety, or alertness. Those possible consequences remain to be investigated, and additional research is needed to determine whether the same dopamine changes occur in people.

Dopamine is often associated with pleasure and motivation, but it also helps regulate wakefulness and other essential brain functions. Its presence is not harmful on its own. What matters is whether its activity remains appropriately balanced.

According to Rocha, difficulties could arise if dopamine remains unusually elevated when the brain should be preparing for sleep. Such changes could also disrupt the balance between dopamine and other neurotransmitters, potentially affecting how the nervous system regulates activity and rest.

Sources indicate that another notable finding involved serotonin, a neurotransmitter that has long been investigated for its possible role in fatigue. Despite the substantial changes in dopamine, the researchers detected no significant differences in serotonin levels between the animals.

This result challenges the long-standing idea that serotonin alone is primarily responsible for excessive fatigue. Instead, the findings suggest that changes in dopamine regulation may also deserve attention when scientists investigate the biological effects of overtraining.

Why Recovery Is Essential for the Brain and Body.

Although the connection between these chemical changes and symptoms such as insomnia or anxiety has not yet been established in humans, the findings reinforce the importance of allowing sufficient time for recovery.

Sources indicate that excessive training without adequate rest can undermine the benefits of exercise, contributing to reduced performance, persistent muscle pain, and problems with immune function. The fresh results suggest that changes in brain chemistry may be another important part of this process.

Recent findings suggest that for recreational exercisers and professional athletes alike, the researchers emphasize that training should be balanced with appropriate recovery and expert guidance. Increasing workout intensity does not necessarily produce better results if the body is not given enough time to adapt.

Rocha also conducted research during a postdoctoral fellowship at the School of Applied Sciences (FCA) of the State University of Campinas (UNICAMP) in Limeira. This work included an internship at the University of Michigan in the United States, where he currently works as a researcher.

In a recent development, additional funding came from a Thematic Project led by Silva, a postdoctoral fellowship awarded to Ana Paula Pinto, and a direct doctorate scholarship supporting João Pedro Floriano. Both Pinto and Floriano are affiliated with EEFERP-USP.

The team is now participating in a latest international research project aimed at identifying which biological systems first begin to show signs of strain when exercise exceeds the level at which it normally produces beneficial adaptations. Understanding these early warning signals could help scientists determine when productive training begins to become harmful.
